Working notes:
- Routing options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.
- C has been chosen many times (REQ-2400/01/02/04/05/06/07/08/09) and was rejected every time as invalid. Do not select C.
- Only successful outcome so far: REQ-2403, large refund from north region with “client has been asking about this twice already” → B priority desk accepted.
- A standard queue has not been tested/accepted in observed data.
- Unclear signals: sender name/team, region, size, request type, and phrases like “same as last month,” “regional office,” “scanned, not typed,” or “second attempt” have not reliably indicated C; C still failed.
- Tentative rule: avoid C. Use B for high-urgency/large cases similar to REQ-2403; otherwise A may be the safer default until more evidence exists.
- Need more examples to distinguish A vs B for small/routine shipments, invoices, claims, and non-urgent refunds.

Working notes:
- Routing options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.
- C has been selected many times (REQ-2400/01/02/04/05/06/07/08/09) and rejected every time. Do not select C without new evidence.
- Only confirmed successes: refund requests from north region with phrase “Our client has been asking about this twice already” → B accepted. Confirmed for large refund REQ-2403 and small refund REQ-2412.
- B is not generally valid: rejected for shipment north/large/“second attempt” (REQ-2410), invoice south/large/“regional office” (REQ-2414), shipment east/large/“before end of day” (REQ-2417).
- A has not been confirmed successful. Recent A attempts rejected for claim north (REQ-2411), refund east (REQ-2413, REQ-2415), invoice south (REQ-2416), shipment east (REQ-2418, REQ-2419).
- Size is not decisive: the successful B refunds include both large and small. Large/small alone does not determine A vs B.
- Region, sender/team, request type, and phrases such as “second attempt,” “regional office,” “scanned, not typed,” “before end of day,” and “no rush” have not reliably indicated A or B.
- Tentative rule: use B only for refund + north region + “client has been asking about this twice already.” Otherwise evidence is insufficient; avoid C and do not treat A as a safe default.
- Need more successful examples to distinguish A vs B for routine shipments, invoices, claims, and non-urgent refunds.

Working notes:
- Routing: A=standard, B=priority, C=regional, D=invalid. Do not choose C or D. C rejected many times; D rejected REQ-2420, REQ-2425.
- B is confirmed for north-region refunds: large REQ-2403, REQ-2422; small REQ-2412, REQ-2426. Phrase and size are not decisive (“client asking twice” and “Let me know if anything is missing” both worked).
- B is confirmed for north-region claims with “Our client has been asking about this twice already”: small REQ-2421, REQ-2424, REQ-2427. Unknown for north claims without that phrase.
- A is not a safe default. Recent A rejections: north shipment large “client asking twice” REQ-2423; north refund large “Let me know…” REQ-2428; north shipment small “Same as…” REQ-2429. Earlier A rejected for claim/refund/invoice/shipment.
- B is not generally valid. Rejected for shipment north large “second attempt” REQ-2410; invoice south large “regional office” REQ-2414; shipment east large “before end of day” REQ-2417. So B only within confirmed north refund/claim patterns.
- Size, sender/team, and many phrases (“second attempt,” “regional office,” “before end of day,” “no rush,” “Let me know…,” “Same as…”) do not alone determine A vs B.
- Need more successes for shipments, invoices, non-north requests, and north claims without the key phrase.

Working notes:

- A not safe default. A rejected for: north shipment large “client asking twice” REQ-2423; north refund large “Let me know…” REQ-2428; north shipment small “Same as…” REQ-2429; south invoice large “No rush…” REQ-2432; east refund large “before end of day” REQ-2436; north shipment large “Flagging…” REQ-2437/2438; east refund small “Flagging…” REQ-2439.
- B not general. Rejected: north shipment large “second attempt” REQ-2410; south invoice large “regional office” REQ-2414; east shipment large “before end of day” REQ-2417. So B only in confirmed north refund/claim patterns.

- Need more data for shipments, invoices, non-north requests, and north claims outside known phrases.
